Vous marchez toute la nuit sur le chemin: You walk all night along the towpath, beneath poplars that creak in the wind. The river flows on your left, wide and black. On your right, rapeseed fields gone back to waste ground, and farms with their shutters closed.
Théo marche devant, comme toujours, une: Théo walks ahead, as always, a map in his head.
Maëlle ne lâche pas la main de son fils,: Maëlle doesn’t let go of her son’s hand, even when the path narrows.
Kaz porte le sac le plus lourd, et ne se: Kaz carries the heaviest bag, and doesn’t complain.
Inès ouvre la marche avec son arbalète,: Inès leads the way with her crossbow, just as she did underground.
Nour ne dit rien. Elle compte ses pas à: Nour says nothing. She counts her steps under her breath.
Personne ne marche à vos côtés. Le bruit: No one walks beside you. The sound of your footsteps is the only human sound for miles.
Vers quatre heures du matin, le chemin e: Around four in the morning, the path is cut off. A horde is crossing the towpath from one field to the other, slowly, like a herd going down to drink. Dozens of figures, a hundred metres ahead of you.
Faire tinter doucement la cloche du Berg: Ring the Shepherd’s bell softly from the field, to draw the horde away.
Se coucher dans le fossé et attendre qu’: Lie down in the ditch and wait for them to pass.
Foncer à travers les traînards avant que: Charge through the stragglers before the bulk of the horde turns round.
Un Muet se retourne. Puis un autre. Puis: A Mute turns round. Then another. Then the whole herd turns its head towards you.
Trois traînards de la horde vous barrent: Three stragglers from the horde block your way along the towpath.
Vous vous retrouvez dans le fossé, à moi: You end up in the ditch, half in the water, under a bramble hedge. The horde has passed over you. You don’t know how you’re still alive, and you don’t have time to think about it.
You set off again downstream, limping.
Le soleil est déjà haut quand vous arriv: The sun is already high when you arrive. Half the crowd has gone through, the gangway is half raised. You are late, and here, lateness has a price.
The dawn of the seventh day breaks.
L’écluse de Morvan. Deux portes d’acier,: Morvan Lock. Two steel gates, a hundred-metre basin, a lock-keeper’s house with blue shutters. And in the basin, the Destinée: a tanker barge repainted white, as long as a tower block lying on its side, a red caduceus painted on its funnel.
Devant l’écluse, une double grille de ba: In front of the lock, a double fence of barbed wire. And in front of the fence, a crowd. Sixty, eighty people perhaps, come from everywhere, with suitcases, children, dogs, old people in wheelbarrows. They have been waiting since nightfall.
Sur une plateforme, un homme en combinai: On a platform, a man in grey overalls speaks into a megaphone: Captain Rousset. “Carriers and their families, to the left. Blood test compulsory. Everyone else, we are sorry. Limited capacity.” He repeats it. He repeats it again.
À côté de lui, une femme en blouse blanc: Beside him, a woman in a white coat, arms folded, looks at the crowd the way one looks at a packed waiting room. Dr Sorel.
Un camion arrive par la route du pont, k: A lorry comes in along the bridge road, its horn stuck. On the flatbed, cages. In one cage, Théo. He sees you. He looks away.
Vous êtes arrivé à l’écluse après l’aube: You reached the lock after dawn.
Observer l’écluse et la barge avant d’ag: Watch the lock and the barge before acting.
L’écluse est manœuvrée à la main depuis: The lock is worked by hand from the lock-keeper’s house: the power is cut.
Ask to speak to Dr Sorel.
Se mêler à la foule qui attend devant la: Blend into the crowd waiting at the fence.
Faire le tour par la maison de l’éclusie: Go round by the lock-keeper’s house.
Rejoindre La Mouette, amarrée en aval de: Join La Mouette, moored downstream of the lock.
Aborder l’homme seul au fond de la foule: Approach the man standing alone at the back of the crowd. You know that build.
La foule sent la sueur, la fumée et la p: The crowd smells of sweat, smoke and fear. People talk in low voices, as if in a hospital waiting room. No one argues: everyone has understood that the slightest scene would get the fence closed.
Une femme vous attrape la manche. Claire: A woman catches your sleeve. Claire Delmas, a former piano teacher, in her forties, a six-year-old child in her arms. The boy’s cheeks are too red and his eyes too bright.
« Ce n’est pas la Fièvre, souffle-t-elle: “It isn’t the Fever,” she breathes. “He cut himself on barbed wire, three days ago. But they don’t take the sick.” She asks for nothing. She looks at your bag.
Plus loin, un vieil homme distribue ce q: Further on, an old man hands out what is left of his cigarettes to strangers, one by one, wishing each of them good luck. A teenager recites a list of names under his breath, always the same one, so as not to forget it.
Donner une boîte d’antibiotiques pour le: Give a box of antibiotics for little Jules.
Vous avez donné vos antibiotiques à un e: You gave your antibiotics to an unknown child at the fence.
Clean and dress the wound yourself.
Détourner les yeux et retourner vers l’é: Look away and head back towards the lock.
Jules serre les dents pendant que vous t: Jules grits his teeth while you work. He doesn’t cry. When it’s over, he gives you a military salute, very serious, his hand the wrong way round.
Claire Delmas ne dit pas merci. Elle vou: Claire Delmas doesn’t say thank you. She grips your forearm, hard, and repeats your name so she will remember it.
Autour de vous, des gens ont regardé. Un: Around you, people have been watching. A murmur runs along the fence: there is someone here who shares.
La maison aux volets bleus est vide. Sur: The house with the blue shutters is empty. On the kitchen table, a bowl of mouldy coffee and a calendar stopped at March two years ago. In the back room, the sluice mechanism: a great cast-iron wheel, a crank, a locking pawl eaten away by rust.
Le courant est coupé. Pour ouvrir les po: The power is cut. To open the downstream gates, someone will have to turn the crank by hand, for a long time. Unless the pawl is wedged so that the weight of the water does the work on its own, when the time comes.
« Un coin de bois sous le cliquet, et un: “A wooden wedge under the pawl, and a pin to pull out at the last moment,” murmurs Kaz. “The old-timers did that when they were too drunk to turn the wheel.”
Rig the pawl with your tools.
Caler le cliquet à coups de masse et d’é: Wedge the pawl with sledgehammer blows and shoulder.
Go back out without touching anything.
Le cliquet tient, coincé par un coin de: The pawl holds, jammed by an oak wedge and a makeshift pin. When the time comes, all it will take is a tug on a wire from the window, and the water will open the gates for you.
Personne ne saura que c’est vous. C’est: No one will know it was you. That is probably for the best.
Vous avez préparé le cliquet des vannes: You rigged the pawl on the lock’s sluices.
La goupille casse net. Le cliquet retomb: The pin snaps clean. The pawl drops back with a clang that makes the whole crowd outside jump. The crank will have to be turned by hand, like everyone else.
Retourner vers l’écluse, les mains écorc: Head back towards the lock, your hands skinned.
La Mouette est amarrée trois cents mètre: La Mouette is moored three hundred metres downstream, tarpaulined up to the rail. Mother Cazal is smoking her unlit pipe on deck, her eyes on the white barge.
« Je suis venue voir partir le dernier b: “I came to watch the last boat in the world leave. And to sell two or three things to the people who won’t be getting on it.” She taps her pipe. “Business is business.”
« Gaspard est là, dans la foule. Seul. I: “Gaspard is here, in the crowd. Alone. He lost everything at the Iron Bridge. He’s looking for a place, like the others. Funny old world.”
« Rousset garde les clés de la grille su: “Rousset keeps the keys to the fence on him. And he never sleeps. That one’s free.”
Une boîte d’antibiotiques contre 2 ratio: A box of antibiotics for 2 rations.
Saluer la vieille batelière et remonter: Say goodbye to the old boatwoman and head back up to the lock.
Gaspard Lenoir n’a plus de plastron, plu: Gaspard Lenoir no longer has his breastplate, his sledgehammer or his dogs. Just a coat that’s too big and a neck covered in dressings. He recognises you before you are within three metres.
Gaspard Lenoir est venu seul, sans ses h: Gaspard Lenoir has come alone, without his men, in a town coat. The barge isn’t buying anything from him any more; so he has come, like everyone else, to try to buy his place on it. He recognises you before you are within three metres.
« Tiens. Toi. Tu m’as laissé la vie, au: “Well. You. You spared my life, at the Iron Bridge.” He spits on the ground.
« Tiens. La petite bande de la casse. »: “Well. The little gang from the scrapyard.” He spits on the ground.
« Tu viens voir si je fais la queue comm: “Come to see if I’m queuing like the rest? I’m queuing like the rest.”
« Je sais ce que je leur ai vendu. Je sa: “I know what I sold them. I know how much they paid. I know who to.” He looks at Sorel’s white coat, on the other side of the wire. “If anyone wants to hear it from my own mouth, I’ll say it. Not for you. So that bastard Rousset doesn’t sail back up the river with a clean conscience.”
L’emmener jusqu’à la grille pour qu’il p: Take him to the fence so he can talk to Dr Sorel.
Gaspard Lenoir a avoué devant la docteur: Gaspard Lenoir confessed the trade in carriers in front of Dr Sorel.
Gaspard parle à travers les barbelés pen: Gaspard talks through the barbed wire for ten minutes, without raising his voice. The deliveries. The cages. The places on the lower deck. The name of the captain who signed the receipts.
La docteure Sorel ne l’interrompt pas un: Dr Sorel does not interrupt him once. At the end, she takes off her glasses and pinches the bridge of her nose, for a very long time.
On vous fait entrer dans une tente de tr: You are shown into a triage tent beside the fence. Anaïs Sorel is sitting on a crate of medical supplies, a cup of cold coffee in her hands. She is in her forties, with shadows under her eyes halfway down her cheeks, and a voice you recognise at once: the one from the radio.
« C’est vous. L’appel de la capitainerie: “It’s you. The call from the Harbour Master’s Office.” She looks you over. “You came all this way.”
« Les porteurs représentent un humain su: “Carriers make up one human in ten thousand. Their blood contains antibodies nobody else produces. On Ferrand Island, we have a laboratory, generals who are waiting, and a vaccine that doesn’t work yet. With twenty carriers, I can make it work. With twenty carriers, I can save everyone behind that fence, and millions more.”
« Le capitaine pense que la fin justifie: “The captain thinks the end justifies the means. I used to think he was wrong. I don’t know any more. Convince me.”
Lui faire écouter l’enregistrement de la: Play her the recording from the Harbour Master’s Office.
Lui montrer la dernière page du carnet d: Show her the last page of Malik’s notebook.
Lui montrer la circulaire « Confidentiel: Show her the “Confidential” memo found at the hospital.
Lui montrer la lettre de l’Institut adre: Show her the Institute’s letter addressed to Maëlle.
Let Nour tell her about the cage.
Présenter Théo. Pas comme un échantillon: Introduce Théo. Not as a sample: as Théo.
« Je ne savais pas. Je ne voulais pas sa: “I didn’t know. I didn’t want to know.” Sorel puts down her cup. Her hands are shaking. “If you have a proposal to make to the captain, make it in front of me. This time, I won’t keep quiet.”
« Je comprends votre colère. » Elle déto: “I understand your anger.” She looks away. “But I only have your word against the captain’s, and millions of lives in the balance. I’m sorry.”
Le capitaine Rousset descend de sa plate: Captain Rousset comes down from his platform as you approach. He is in his fifties, with a crew cut, a riot shield propped against his leg. Two guards in grey overalls flank the gate in the fence.
« Je connais cette tête-là. La tête de q: “I know that face. The face of someone who has something to sell me or something to hold against me.” He looks at Théo. He sees the scar before Théo has even moved. “Ah. Both, then.”
« Une plaque des Ferrailleurs. » Il sour: “A Scrappers’ tag.” He smiles without joy. “A paid passenger. Board with the delivery.”
« Pas de porteur, pas de passage. C’est: “No carrier, no passage. It’s simple, it’s sad, it’s protocol.”
Derrière vous, la foule s’est tue. Tout: Behind you, the crowd has gone quiet. Everyone is listening.
Théo vous regarde. Il ne dit rien. Il at: Théo looks at you. He says nothing. He is waiting to see what you will do with him.
Glisser la cassette entre les barbelés,: Slip the cassette through the barbed wire, into Dr Sorel’s hands.
Proposer l’Accord : Théo embarque comme: Propose the Accord: Théo boards as a volunteer, under Sorel’s protection, and the whole group with him.
Livrer Théo au capitaine contre des plac: Hand Théo over to the captain in exchange for places for the group.
There will be no going back.
Présenter la plaque de Gaspard et monter: Show Gaspard’s tag and board with the delivery.
Prendre le mégaphone et diffuser l’enreg: Take the megaphone and play the recording to the whole crowd.
Turn your back on the Destinée.
« Théo monte à bord. Pas dans une cage,: “Théo goes aboard. Not in a cage, not in a delivery log: as a passenger. He will give his blood if and when he decides to, under Dr Sorel’s responsibility. Those with him go aboard with him. And the Scrappers’ cages won’t earn you a single place ever again.”
« Et pourquoi j’accepterais ça ? »: “And why would I agree to that?”
« Parce que sans moi, capitaine, il n’y: “Because without me, Captain, there is no vaccine.” Sorel has stepped up beside you. Her voice no longer shakes. “And because I’ve heard the cassette, like half your crew, who are listening right now behind the bulkhead.”
Rousset regarde ses gardes. Ses gardes r: Rousset looks at his guards. His guards look at their boots. He understands before he has decided.
« J’y vais », dit Théo. Il le dit à vous: “I’ll go,” says Théo. He says it to you, not to Rousset. “But not as a parcel.”
« Embarquez. » Un seul mot, et il remont: “Board.” A single word, and he climbs back onto his platform without looking round.
L’Accord est conclu : Théo embarque comm: The Accord is made: Théo boards as a free passenger, under Sorel’s protection.
Vous arrachez le mégaphone de sa platefo: You snatch the megaphone from its platform before anyone understands. You press the dictaphone against the mic. And Captain Rousset’s voice rolls across the whole lock, metallic, relentless:
« … huit places sur le pont inférieur. L: “… eight places on the lower deck. The rest of the contingent will be sorted at the fence. The rest is negotiable.”
Il y a une seconde de silence absolu. Pu: There is a second of absolute silence. Then the crowd throws itself at the fence. The barbed wire gives way under the weight. The guards fall back, fire into the air, fall back again. Rousset does not fall back. He picks up his shield and walks straight at you.
« Capitaine ! Arrêtez ! » La voix de Sor: “Captain! Stop!” Sorel’s voice, somewhere behind. He doesn’t hear her.
Rousset lève son bouclier. « Je l’ai dit: Rousset raises his shield. “I told you: it’s protocol.”
Le capitaine Rousset, bouclier levé. Il: Captain Rousset, shield raised. He can call guards by radio.
La foule a submergé les gardes. Rousset: The crowd has overwhelmed the guards. Rousset stands alone before you, in the middle of the chaos.
Rousset est seul : ses gardes sont débor: Rousset is alone: his guards are swamped by the crowd. He is off balance.
C’est le bruit qui les a attirés. Les cr: It was the noise that drew them. The shouting, the engines, the gunshots perhaps. On the towpath, upstream, a grey tide is advancing between the poplars: hundreds of Mutes, in silence, with that immense clicking, like hail on a tin roof.
Pour quitter l’écluse, la Destinée doit: To leave the lock, the Destinée has to go down into the basin and wait for the downstream gates to open. But the power has been cut since dawn, and the sluices are worked by hand, from the lock-keeper’s house, at the edge of the path. Where the horde will arrive first.
Douze minutes de manivelle. Quelqu’un do: Twelve minutes of cranking. Someone has to stay.
« C’est mon métier, ça. » Kaz retrousse: “That’s my trade, that is.” Kaz rolls up his sleeves. “Thirty years I’ve been turning lock cranks. I can do it with my eyes shut.”
À la tête de la marée avance une silhoue: At the head of the tide comes an enormous figure, in black riot gear, helmet and shin guards. The Colossus. It is walking straight towards the lock-keeper’s house.
Grimper sur la passerelle et faire sonne: Climb onto the gangway and ring the Shepherd’s bell to lead the horde away from the river.
La cloche du Berger a emmené la horde lo: The Shepherd’s bell led the horde away from the lock.
Tirer le fil de fer depuis la passerelle: Pull the wire from the gangway: the rigged pawl gives, and the water opens the gates on its own.
Le cliquet préparé a ouvert les portes d: The rigged pawl opened the lock gates without anyone having to stay.
Kaz est resté à la manivelle de l’écluse: Kaz stayed at the lock crank. He didn’t come back.
Tenir le chemin devant la maison de l’éc: Hold the path in front of the lock-keeper’s house, facing the Colossus, while someone turns the crank.
Vous avez libéré Théo du camion de Gaspa: You freed Théo from Gaspard’s lorry.
Derrière vous, la manivelle grince. Deva: Behind you, the crank creaks. Ahead of you, the Colossus advances, and the horde marches in its wake.
Le Colosse de l’écluse. Son armure arrêt: The Colossus of the lock. Its armour stops almost everything: fire and distraction are your best weapons. Hold out for twelve minutes.
La Destinée descend dans le bassin. Les: The Destinée goes down into the basin. The downstream gates open in a roar of water, and the barge glides out onto the open river, all lights out.
Sur la berge, la horde s’éloigne vers le: On the bank, the horde drifts off towards the fields, following a cowbell ringing further and further away. You swim to the barge, and hands haul you aboard.
Un fil de fer tiré depuis la passerelle,: A wire pulled from the gangway, a dull clang in the lock-keeper’s house, and the gates open on their own under the weight of the river. The horde arrives on an empty quay. No one had to stay.
Le Colosse gît en travers du chemin de h: The Colossus lies across the towpath, and the horde, robbed of its leader, has scattered among the poplars.
Sur la berge, la maison de l’éclusier di: On the bank, the lock-keeper’s house disappears beneath the grey tide. Right up to the last moment, you hear the crank creaking. Then nothing. Kaz held out his twelve minutes.
Trois jours plus tard, la barge accoste: Three days later, the barge docks at Ferrand Island. Théo is the first down the gangway, without handcuffs, without an escort, Dr Sorel’s hand resting on his shoulder. Not the left shoulder. The other one.
Sorel tient parole. Les porteurs de l’îl: Sorel keeps her word. The island’s carriers now have a room, a name on the door and the right to say no. Théo says yes, three times a week, for a blood sample. The rest of the time, he draws the map of the island.
Six mois plus tard, le premier lot de va: Six months later, the first batch of vaccine leaves the laboratory. They call it batch T, and nobody says why.
Maëlle a pris en charge l’infirmerie du: Maëlle took charge of the lower-deck sickbay from the very first evening. She still doesn’t sleep much. But when she sleeps, she sleeps, and it’s you she trusts to watch over Théo in the meantime.
Maëlle soigne, compte les doses, parle p: Maëlle tends the sick, counts the doses, says little. She has never quite forgiven you for the letter, or the rest. She stays polite. It’s her way of keeping her distance.
Maëlle n’est pas là. Sa lampe s’est étei: Maëlle isn’t there. Her lamp went out at the far end of a gallery in the ossuary, and sometimes, at night, Théo still looks around for her.
Kaz tient la barre du pont arrière, la n: Kaz takes the helm on the aft deck at night. He sings in Polish for the children who can’t sleep. He sings out of tune. Nobody complains. One evening, he told you that Irena would have loved the sea.
Kaz travaille dur et parle peu. Il vous: Kaz works hard and says little. Sometimes he looks at you like someone still waiting to be judged.
On raconte au port qu’un grand Polonais: At the port they say that a big Pole with a face painted in engine grease left the Scrappers the night Gaspard fell. No one knows where he went.
Kaz porte toujours la peinture des Ferra: Kaz still wears the Scrappers’ paint. They say he has become Gaspard’s right-hand man. They also say he refuses to touch the cages.
De Kaz, il ne reste qu’une manivelle tor: All that is left of Kaz is a bent crank, which someone has welded to the parapet of Morvan Lock.
Inès a recopié le carnet de son frère à: Inès has copied out her brother’s notebook in ink, page after page, so that no one can say he never existed. On the island, she maps the coastline. She shows you every new map before anyone else.
Inès est descendue au premier village du: Inès got off at the first village on the river. “Others are waiting under the city.” She shook your hand, once, firmly. She isn’t the type to look back.
Inès est retournée sous Valombre. Les pa: Inès went back beneath Valombre. The smugglers say she now knows every gallery, and that she never asks for anything in return any more.
Nour a demandé à voir les cages vides de: Nour asked to see the empty cages in the hold. She looked at them for a long time, then asked for them to be thrown overboard. It was done. She and Théo are inseparable now.
Nour est arrivée à l’ossuaire avec les a: Nour reached the ossuary with the other prisoners from the scrapyard. Hélène entered her in the register under the “arrivals” column. It is the only column that counts.
Odilon sonne toujours les cloches, chaqu: Odilon still rings the bells, every evening at seven, for those still walking in the city.
Les cloches de Saint-Clair n’ont plus ja: The bells of Saint-Clair never rang again. No one knows what became of the old man in the bell tower.
Les Veilleurs ont tenu. L’eau est claire: The Watchers held. The water is clear, the children still recite their times tables, and Hélène Vasseur has added your name in the margin of her register.
Gaspard Lenoir tient une buvette sur le: Gaspard Lenoir runs a refreshment stall on the Iron Bridge. He sells nothing but petrol and bad coffee now. He tells anyone who will listen that he was conned by a bigger thief than himself.
Gaspard Lenoir a témoigné, pour une fois: Gaspard Lenoir testified, under oath for once. They say he is almost proud of it.
La famille Delmas a survécu. Le petit Ju: The Delmas family survived. Little Jules has kept the habit of giving you a military salute every time he passes you.
Vous, {nom}, vous avez un lit, une fenêt: You, {nom}, have a bed, a window onto the sea, and a job: escorting the barges that go back up the river to fetch the others. There are still many of them. There always will be.
La Destinée descend dans le bassin, et l: The Destinée goes down into the basin, and the downstream gates open in a roar of water. Rousset is locked in his own cabin, handcuffed to his bunk. No one knows yet what will be done with him.
Au loin, une cloche de vache emmène la h: In the distance, a cowbell leads the horde off towards the fields. You swim to the barge to cheers.
Le cliquet préparé lâche au bon moment,: The rigged pawl gives at just the right moment, and the gates open under the weight of the river. No one had to stay at the crank.
Le Colosse gît en travers du chemin de h: The Colossus lies across the towpath, and the horde, robbed of its leader, scatters beneath the poplars.
La maison de l’éclusier disparaît sous l: The lock-keeper’s house disappears beneath the grey tide. Right up to the last moment, the crank creaks. Kaz held out his twelve minutes.
À bord, la foule de la grille a tout env: On board, the crowd from the fence has overrun everything: the gangways, the holds, the upper deck. Eighty bunks for two hundred people. People sleep in shifts, share everything, argue about everything.
La docteure Sorel est restée à bord. Ell: Dr Sorel stayed on board. She spoke in front of everyone on the first evening, to say what she knew, and what she had agreed not to know. Then she opened her laboratory to the carriers, and this time she asked them.
Théo dort dans le poste de pilotage, rou: Théo sleeps in the wheelhouse, rolled up in a blanket, next to you. He doesn’t know yet whether he will give his blood. He has time to decide. That’s all he asked for.
L’île Ferrand vous attend à trois jours: Ferrand Island lies three days’ sailing away. No one knows how the Institute will receive a mutinous barge. You’ll see. You’ve seen worse.
Au matin, quelqu’un a repeint le nom sur: In the morning, someone has repainted the name on the hull. It no longer reads “La Destinée”. It reads, in clumsy letters: “Ours”.
Vous fermez la porte de la maison de l’é: You shut the door of the lock-keeper’s house behind you and push the wardrobe against it. Then you take the crank in both hands, and you turn.
Un tour. Dix tours. Cent tours. Par la f: One turn. Ten turns. A hundred turns. Through the window, you see the Destinée slowly sinking into the basin. You see Théo, on deck, searching for you. You raise your hand. He raises his.
Par la fenêtre, vous voyez la Destinée d: Through the window, you see the Destinée slowly sinking into the basin, laden with all those who should never have got on board, and who are getting on anyway.
Les coups contre la porte commencent à l: The blows against the door begin in the fourth minute. The clicking of teeth, through the wood, like hail. The wardrobe shifts back a centimetre, then another.
À la douzième minute, les portes aval s’: In the twelfth minute, the downstream gates open in a roar of water. The barge glides out onto the open river. You let go of the crank. Your hands are bleeding. You sit down on the floor, your back against the wardrobe, and you listen to the water.
Sur l’île Ferrand, dans le hall du labor: On Ferrand Island, in the laboratory’s entrance hall, there is a copper plaque. Théo had it engraved with the first money he was given: “{nom}, keeper of Morvan Lock. Twelve minutes.”
Rousset fait signe à ses gardes. Ils pre: Rousset signals to his guards. They take Théo by the arms. He doesn’t struggle. He simply looks at you, until the door of the medical cabin closes on him.
Maëlle hurle. C’est le premier son qu’el: Maëlle screams. It is the first sound she has made since Valombre. She throws herself at the guards, and they take her aboard with her son, because the protocol provides for families. She will never speak to you again.
Vous montrez la plaque de Gaspard. On vo: You show Gaspard’s tag. You are taken aboard with the delivery. In the lorry, there are cages. In one cage, there is Théo. He doesn’t look at you. He will never look at you again.
On vous donne une couchette sur le pont: You are given a bunk on the lower deck, a blanket, a mess tin of hot soup. The first in months. It tastes of iron.
À l’île Ferrand, le vaccin marchera, ou: On Ferrand Island, the vaccine will work, or it won’t. You won’t find out straight away. You will only know that a boy who drew maps on the walls of a pharmacy now lives in a windowless room, with a number on the door.
Vous êtes en vie. Vous êtes à bord. Vous: You are alive. You are on board. You have paid the price of passage, and you are not the one who paid it.
L’écluse est ouverte. Le bassin est vide: The lock is open. The basin is empty. On the quay, overturned barbed wire, split suitcases, a megaphone abandoned in a puddle.
Loin en aval, sur le fleuve gris, un poi: Far downstream, on the grey river, a white dot grows smaller. The Destinée left on time. It waited for no one.
Théo regarde le point blanc jusqu’à ce q: Théo watches the white dot until it disappears. Then he looks at you. He doesn’t blame you for anything. That is almost worse.
Quelque part derrière ce point blanc, Th: Somewhere behind that white dot, Théo is in a cage, on his way to the island. You have arrived too late to get him back.
Remonter vers l’ossuaire Saint-Roch et r: Head back up to Saint-Roch Ossuary and join the Watchers.

Vous regardez la barge blanche, le caduc: You look at the white barge, the red caduceus, the crowd, the barbed wire. And you understand that you don’t want to get on that boat. Not at that price. Not with those people.
Théo vous regarde, puis regarde la barge: Théo looks at you, then at the barge, then at you again. He slips his hand into yours.
Dans le camion des Ferrailleurs, Théo es: In the Scrappers’ lorry, Théo is still in a cage. There is nothing you can do for him, or you have chosen that there is nothing you can do.

Théo marche à côté de vous jusqu’à la gr: Théo walks beside you up to the gate. Hélène Vasseur is waiting for him. She holds out a Saint-Roch medal, and he puts it round his neck without a word.
Maëlle dirige l’infirmerie de l’ossuaire: Maëlle runs the ossuary’s sickbay. She has finally slept through a whole night.
Hélène tient parole : Théo n’est pas une: Hélène keeps her word: Théo is not merchandise here. He is one Watcher among others. The Watchers make their own serum, with equipment stolen from Delorme Hospital and help from Sister Prudence. It doesn’t work. Not yet. One day, perhaps.
Odilon Brac has come down to live with them. He rings the ossuary’s bells every evening, for the children.
Kaz a remis en marche une vieille écluse: Kaz has got an old hand-operated lock working again on the Tanners’ Canal, “to keep my hand in”. The Watchers call him the Captain. He pretends to hate it.
Inès est redevenue passeuse. Mais elle n: Inès has become a smuggler again. But she no longer charges anyone. On the walls of the Chalk Gallery, a new arrow bears an I and an M intertwined.
Nour apprend à lire avec les enfants de: Nour is learning to read with the ossuary’s children. She is already better than everyone at mental arithmetic. She still wears the key to her cage around her neck.
Vous, {nom}, vous reprenez le métier des: You, {nom}, take up the smugglers’ trade. You guide those who want to reach the river through the Labyrinth, and you bring back those who want to stay. The Destinée never comes back through Morvan. No one here misses it.
Vous trouvez une barque à fond plat amar: You find a flat-bottomed boat moored under the willows, with two oars and a can of water. You push it out into the current, and the river carries you downstream, away from the lock, away from the barge, away from Valombre.
Théo est assis à l’avant. Il dessine la: Théo sits in the bow. He sketches the passing bank on a torn-out page. He doesn’t ask you where you are going. You don’t know either.
Vous ne regardez pas le camion des Ferra: You don’t look at the Scrappers’ lorry. You will never look at a lorry the same way again.
Ceux qui sont restés avec vous rament à: Those who stayed with you take turns at the oars. In the evenings, you put in on nameless banks, and tell each other about Valombre like a story that happened to someone else.
Le fleuve est long. Il traverse des vill: The river is long. It runs through dead towns, forests, plains where the grass has taken back the motorways. Somewhere, perhaps, there are other people, other refuges, other rules. You’ll see.
Vous êtes en vie, {nom}. Dans ce monde-l: You are alive, {nom}. In this world, that is already a victory. It isn’t quite an ending.

Dans le registre de la Destinée, à la da: In the Destinée’s log, under the date of the seventh day, a guard will later write a line in pencil: “Incident at the fence. One dead. Unidentified.”
